title: PCSX2 reorganizes RetroAchievements leaderboards around subsets and active state
summary: Expandable active and inactive groups plus a subset sidebar make large leaderboard sets navigable, while shared helpers align their behavior with the achievement screen.
heroAlt: Source evidence from PCSX2 pull request #14402: Achievements: Group leaderboards by subset and tracking state

sourceLabels.pcsx2-pr-14402: Achievements: Group leaderboards by subset and tracking state

blocks.text: One long list hides which leaderboard is currently relevant

Games can expose many RetroAchievements leaderboards and can divide content into subsets. Presenting every board in a single sequence mixes actively tracked challenges with inactive ones and gives no strong sense of which subset owns an entry. Pull request #14402 reorganizes the pause-menu view so players first see meaningful groups and, where required, a separate subset navigation area.
Tracking state creates expandable leaderboard groups

Boards are sorted into sections such as active and inactive rather than left in one pile. Players can open or close those groups, making currently running challenges easier to find without deleting access to the rest. Games with subset content gain a left sidebar similar to the achievements view, and common logic is moved into helpers so both screens handle grouping and subset presentation consistently.
Confirm and Cancel replace lateral D-pad subset switching

The implementation avoids using D-pad directions to change subsets. Confirm enters or selects subset content and Cancel returns, leaving directional input to navigate the current list and sidebar predictably. That choice matters in controller-first UI: a left or right press used to inspect a leaderboard should not silently replace the entire data set. Keyboard behavior still needs to follow the same focus model.
Gran Turismo 4 supplies a real multi-subset test

Open achievements and leaderboards for Gran Turismo 4, switch every subset, expand and collapse active and inactive groups, and verify tracked boards move groups as state changes. Repeat with a game that has no subsets and one with empty groups. Test keyboard and controller, pause and resume, and reopen the menu to confirm state is not stale. Shared helper changes require checking the achievements screen too, not only the new leaderboard layout.
The screen now separates two questions: which content subset is open, and which leaderboards inside it are currently active.
